title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Mars
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Mars, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his fire and his knife. Mars is the planet of the knife and the forge: surgery, bloodletting, the taming of wild beasts, the smithy's fire, war, and banditry fall under him, with army camps, battlefields, and places of judgment among his locations. His seat in the body is the gallbladder, the source of yellow bile and heat, and bright red is his color. A waxing Moon facing him by aspect is counted a misfortune; his is the figure the lunar doctrine watches hardest.
